sights.w: SeaWorld's flagship marine park (1973) — Mako, Kraken, Manta, Pipeline and Penguin Trek coasters plus orca, dolphin and penguin habitats; the anchor of the I-Drive/SeaWorld district (Wikipedia; SeaWorld official).
sights.k: theme park marine animals coasters family icon

sights.w: Orlando's luxury mall (2002) — Chanel, Gucci, Louis Vuitton and an Apple store under a glass-and-steel Millenia rotunda; a fixture of international-visitor shopping trips (Wikipedia; mall official).
"The jewel of downtown Orlando": Joseph Ange's 11-storey 1923 Angebilt Hotel by Murry S. King — rooftop garden, WLOF radio on the mezzanine; NRHP-listed (Wikipedia; CRA historical marker).

sights.address: Lake Eola Heights (north/east of Lake Eola), Orlando, FL 32801
sights.w: One of Orlando's oldest, most architecturally mixed neighbourhoods — ~500 historic bungalows, Colonial Revivals and Queen Annes on brick streets above Lake Eola; NRHP 1992 and a city historic preservation district (Wikipedia; City of Orlando).
sights.k: historic neighborhood nrhp architecture walk free

sights.address: General Hutchison Pkwy (between US 17-92 and SR 427), Longwood, FL
sights.w: Site of The Senator, a ~3,500-year-old bald cypress — once the largest in the US — that burned in 2012; the park keeps its remains, a boardwalk to 'Lady Liberty' and The Phoenix, a clone grown from it (Wikipedia; Seminole County).
sights.k: nature tree boardwalk park free history
